verses.sanskrit:
वैशम्पायन उवाच।
              वनं गतेषु पार्थेषु निर्जितेषु दुरोदरे। धृतराष्ट्रं महाराज तदा चिन्ता समाविशत्॥१॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said At the departure of the Pandavas to the forest after being defeated at dice, the great king Dhritarashtra was afflicted with great anxiety.

verses.sanskrit: एतत्सर्वं सभापर्वं मयाख्यातं महर्षयः। अध्यायाः सप्ततिर्ज्ञ्रेयास्तथा द्वौ चात्र संख्यया॥१॥
verses.english: Vaishampayana said At the departure of the Pandavas to the forest after being defeated at dice, the great king Dhritarashtra was afflicted with great anxiety.

verses.sanskrit: तं चिन्तयानमासीनं धृतराष्ट्रं जनेश्वरम्। निःश्वसन्तमनेकाग्रमिति होवाच सञ्जयः॥२॥
verses.english: When the ruler of men, Dhritarashtra was thus seated in anxiety and restlessness and sighing in grief, Sanjaya came to him and spoke thus.

verses.sanskrit: श्लोकानां द्वे सहस्रे तु सप्तश्लोकशतानि च। श्लोकाश्चैकादश तथा पर्वण्यस्मिन्प्रकीर्तिताः॥२॥
verses.english: When the ruler of men, Dhritarashtra was thus seated in anxiety and restlessness and sighing in grief, Sanjaya came to him and spoke thus.

verses.sanskrit: अवाप्य वसुसम्पूर्णां वसुधां वसुधाधिप। प्रव्राज्य पाण्डवान्राज्याद्राजन्किमनुशोचसि॥३॥
verses.english: Sanjaya said O lord of the world, you have (now) obtained the whole earth with all its wealth; you have banished the Pandavas, why then do you grieve so?

verses.sanskrit:
धृतराष्ट्र उवाच।
              अशोच्यत्वं कुतस्तेषां येषां वैरं भविष्यति। पाण्डवैर्युद्धशौण्डैर्हि बलवद्भिर्महारथैः॥४॥
verses.english: Dhritarashtra said What have they not to grieve for who will have to meet in battle those foremost of heroes, the Pandavas those great car warriors aided by allies.

verses.sanskrit:
सञ्जय उवाच।
              तवेदं सुकृतं राजन्महद्वैरमुपस्थितम्। विनाशो येन लोकस्य सानुबन्धो भविष्यति॥५॥
verses.english: Sanjaya said O king, this is assuredly a great act of yours, this great hostility which is inevitable and which will cause the destruction of the whole world.

verses.sanskrit: वार्यमाणो हि भीष्मेण द्रोणेन विदुरेण च। पाण्डवानां प्रियां भार्यां द्रौपदीं धर्मचारिणीम्॥६॥
verses.english: Bhishma, Drona, Karna and Kripa, the lord (Yudhishthira) also met the son of Drona (Ashvathama) he duly saluted and embraced all of them and was saluted and embraced by them in return.

verses.sanskrit: प्राहिणोदानयेहेति पुत्रो दुर्योधनस्तव। सूतपुत्रं सुमन्दात्मा निर्लज्जः प्रातिकामिनम्॥७॥
verses.english: Forbidden by Bhisma, Drona, and Vidura, your wicked minded and shameless son, Duryodhana sent his Pratikamin, born in the Suta caste, commanding him to bring into the Sabha the beloved and virtuous wife of the Pandavas.

verses.sanskrit: यस्मै देवाः प्रयच्छन्ति पुरुषाय पराभवम्। बुद्धिं तस्यापकर्षन्ति सोऽवाचीतानि पश्यति॥८॥
verses.english: The celestial first deprive that man of his reason to whom they ordain defeat and disgrace. It is for this, he sees every thing in a strange light.

verses.sanskrit: बुद्धौ कलुषभूतायां विनाशे समुपस्थिते। अनयो नयसङ्काशो हृदयान्नापसर्पति॥९॥
verses.english: When destruction is at hand, evil, appearing as good to the mind polluted by sin, remains stuck to it. That which is improper appears as proper, and that which is proper appears as improper to a man overwhelmed by destruction. And this he (always) likes.

verses.sanskrit: अनर्थाश्चार्थरूपेण अर्थाश्चानर्थरूपिणः। उत्तिष्ठन्ति विनाशाय नूनं तच्चास्य रोचते॥१०॥
न कालो दण्डमुद्यम्य शिरः कृन्तति कस्यचित्। कालस्य बलमेतावद्विपरीतार्थदर्शनम्॥११॥
verses.english: The Time that brings on destruction does not come with upraised club to smash one's head. Peculiarity of Time is this that it makes a man see evil in good and good in evil.

verses.sanskrit: आसादितमिदं घोरं तुमुलं लोमहर्षणम्। पाञ्चालीमपकर्षद्भिः सभामध्ये तपस्विनीम्॥१२॥
verses.english: The wretches have brought on themselves this fearful, wholesale and horrible destruction by dragging into the Sabha the ascetic princess of Panchala.

verses.sanskrit: अयोनिजां रूपवतीं कुले जातां विभावसोः। को नु तां सर्वधर्मज्ञां परिभूय यशस्विनीम्॥१३॥
verses.english: Who else than that false player at dice (Duryodhana) could bring into the Sabha with insults the daughter of Drupada, possessing beauty and intelligence, being conversant with every rule of morality and duty, and sprung not from any woman's womb but from the sacred fire. That beautiful lady was in her season covered with blood.

verses.sanskrit: पर्यानयेत्सभामध्ये विना दुर्द्यूतदेविनम्। स्त्रीधर्मिणी वरारोहा शोणितेन परिप्लुता॥१४॥
एकवस्त्राथ पाञ्चाली पाण्डवानभ्यवैक्षत। हृतस्वान्हृतराज्यांश्च हृतवस्त्रान्हृतश्रियः॥१५॥
verses.english: And in one cloth. Panchali (Draupadi) saw the Pandavas, plunged in slavery and robbed of their wealth, of their kingdom, of their attire, of their beauty, and of every object of enjoyment. Bound by the tie of virtue, they were then unable to exert their prowess.

verses.sanskrit: विहीनान्सर्वकामेभ्यो दासभावमुपागतान्। धर्मपाशपरिक्षिप्तानशक्तानिव विक्रमे॥१६॥
क्रुद्धां चानर्हतीं कृष्णां दुःखितां कुरुसंसदि। दुर्योधनश्च कर्णश्च कटुकान्यभ्यभाषताम्॥१७॥

इति सर्वमिदं राजन्नाकुलं प्रतिभाति मे।
              धृतराष्ट्र उवाच।
              तस्याः कृपणचक्षुर्भ्यां प्रदह्येतापि मेदिनी॥१८॥
verses.english: In the midst of the Kuru assembly, Duryodhana and Karna spoke cruel and harsh words to the distressed and enraged Krishna (Draupadi) who did not deserve such treatment.

verses.sanskrit: अपि शेषं भवेदद्य पुत्राणां मम सञ्जय। भरतानां स्त्रियः सर्वा गान्धार्या सह सङ्गताः॥१९॥
verses.english: Dhritarashtra said O Sanjaya, the glances of the affected Draupadi may consume the whole world. Is their any chance of any of my son's living?

verses.sanskrit: प्राकोशन्भैरवं तत्र दृष्ट्वा कृष्णां सभागताम्। धर्मिष्ठां धर्मपत्नीं च रूपयौवनशालिनीम्॥२०॥
verses.english: The ladies of the Bharata race, with Gandhari, seeing the virtuous, young and beautiful Krishna (Draupadi), the wedded wife (of the Pandavas), dragged into court wept aloud. They are even now weeping every day along with all (my) subjects.
verses.bhavadeepa: शेषं हतावशेषं कतिपयानामेकस्य वा जीवनं भविष्यतीत्यर्थः ॥१९॥

verses.sanskrit: प्रजाभिःसह सङ्गम्य ह्यनुशोचन्ति नित्यशः। अग्निहोत्राणि सायाह्ने च चाहूयन्त सर्वशः॥२१॥
verses.english: Enraged at the persecution on Draupadi, all the Brahmanas refrained from performing the Agnihotra in the evening.

verses.sanskrit: ब्राह्मणाः कुपिताश्चासन्द्रौपद्याः परिकर्षणे। आसीन्निष्ठानको घोरो निर्घातश्च महानभूत्॥२२॥
verses.english: The winds frightful begun to blow as they do at the universal destruction. A fearful thunder storm raged, Metros fell from the sky and devoured the sun, and unseasonably and fearfully alarmed all the people. The fire came blazing out from the chariot house.

verses.sanskrit: दिव उल्काश्चापतन्त राहुश्चार्कमुपाग्रसत्। अपर्वणि महाघोरं प्रजानां जयन्भयम्॥२३॥
verses.bhavadeepa: निष्ठानकः प्रलयदुन्दुभिश्चण्डवात इत्यर्थः । निष्टानक इति पाठेऽपि स एवार्थः निर्घातः वज्रशब्दः ॥२२॥

verses.sanskrit: तथैव रथशालासु प्रादुरासीद्धुताशनः। ध्वजाश्चापि व्यशीर्यन्त भरतानामभूतये॥२४॥
दुर्योधनस्याग्निहोत्रे प्राक्रोशन्भैरवं शिवाः। तास्तदा प्रत्यभाषन्त रासभाः सर्वतो दिशः॥२५॥
verses.english: All their flag staffs fell down, foreboding evil to the Bharatas. Jackals fearfully cried out within the sacred fire chamber of Duryodhana.

verses.sanskrit: प्रातिष्ठत ततो भीष्मो द्रोणेन सह सञ्जय। कृपश्च सोमदत्तश्च बाह्लीकश्च महामनाः॥२६॥
verses.english: Asses from all directions began to bray in response (to the jackal). O Sanjaya, then left the assembly Bhisma, Drona with

verses.sanskrit: ततोऽहमब्रुवं तत्र विदुरेण प्रचोदितः। वरं ददानि कृष्णायै काङ्क्षितं यद्यदिच्छति॥२७॥
verses.english: Kripa, Somadatta, and the high souled Valhika. It was then at the advice of Vidura, I spoke thus (to Draupadi).

verses.sanskrit: अवृणोत्तत्र पाञ्चाली पाण्डवानामदासताम्। सरथान्सधनुष्कांश्चाप्यनुज्ञासिषमप्यहम्॥२८॥
verses.english: "O Krishna, I shall grant you boons whatever you desire to have." Panchali (Draupadi) begged of me the liberation of the Pandavas.

verses.sanskrit: अथाब्रवीन्महाप्राज्ञो विदुरः सर्वधर्मवित्। एतदन्तास्तु भरता यद्वः कृष्णा सभां गता॥२९॥
verses.english: I then set free the Pandavas and commanded them to go away with their cars, bows and arrows. It was then the greatly intelligent Vidura spoke thus.
verses.bhavadeepa: अनुज्ञासिषम् अनुज्ञातवान् । अडभाव आर्षः पाठान्तरे तु सुगमम् ॥२८॥

verses.sanskrit: यैषा पाञ्चालराजस्य सुता सा श्रीरनुत्तमा। पाञ्चाली पाण्डवानेतान्दैवसृष्टोपसर्पति॥३०॥
verses.english: Vidura said This will prove the destruction of the Bharata race, namely the dragging of Krishna into the Sabha. This excellent daughter of the Panchala is Sree (the goddess of wealth) herself.

verses.sanskrit: तस्याः पार्थाः परिक्लेशं न क्षंस्यन्ते ह्यमर्षणाः। वृष्णयो वा महेष्वासाः पाञ्चाला वा महारथाः॥३१॥
verses.english: Of celestial origin, Panchali is the wedded wife of the Pandavas. The wrathful sons of Pritha will never forgive the insult offered to her.

verses.sanskrit: तेन सत्याभिसन्धेन वासुदेवेन रक्षिताः। आगमिष्यति बीभत्सुः पञ्चालैः परिवारितः॥३२॥
verses.english: The mighty bowmen of the Vrishni race, and the mighty Panchala car warriors will not suffer this in silence. Supported by Vasudeva (Krishna),

verses.sanskrit: तेषां मध्ये महेष्वासो भीमसेनो महाबलः। आगमिष्यति धुन्वानो गदां दण्डमिवान्तकः॥३३॥
verses.english: Vivatsu (Arjuna) will certainly come back surrounded by the Panchala heroes. Among them, the great bowman and greatly powerful Bhimsena.

verses.sanskrit: ततो गाण्डीवनिर्घोषं श्रुत्वा पार्थस्य धीमतः। गदावेगं च भीमस्य नालं सोढुं नराधिपाः॥३४॥
verses.english: Will also come back whirling his club like Yama himself his mace. There will be no kings who will be able to stand the sound of the Govinda (bow) of the intelligent Partha (Arjuna) and the terrible force of the club of Bhima. Therefore it seems to me to be the best to have peace and not hostility with the sons of Pritha.

verses.sanskrit: तत्र मे रोचते नित्यं पार्थैः साम न विग्रहः। कुरुभ्यो हि सदा मन्ये पाण्डवान्बलवत्तरान्॥३५॥
तथा हि बलवान्राजा जरासन्धो महाद्युतिः। बाहुप्रहरणेनैव भीमेन निहतो युधि॥३६॥
verses.english: The Pandavas are always stronger than the Kurus. The greatly effulgent king Jarasandha.

verses.sanskrit: तस्य ते शम एवास्तु पाण्डवैर्भरतर्षभ। उभयोः पक्षयोर्युक्तं क्रियतामविशङ्कया॥३७॥
verses.english: O great king, without scruples of any kind, unite the two parties. If it is done, you are sure to obtain good fortune."

verses.sanskrit: एवं कृते महाराज परं श्रेयस्त्वमाप्स्यसि। एवं गावल्गणे क्षत्ता धर्मार्थसहितं वचः॥३८॥
verses.english: Dhritarashtra said The son of Gavalgana, Khattwa (Vidura) spoke in words replete with Dharma and Artha. I did not accept his words moved by the affection I bear for my sons.

verses.sanskrit: उक्तवान्न गृहीतं वै मया पुत्रहितैषिणा॥३९॥
